page: Microsoft Azure D16s_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor operating at 4.2 GHz. The instance configuration allocates 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 8 physical cores using multithreading. It is equipped with 64.0 GB of memory, yielding a 4.0 GB per vCPU ratio. The processor integrates 480 MB of L3 cache along with 2 MB of L2 cache per core. Architectural instruction support includes Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX-TILE, AMX-INT8) and AVX-512 vector sets.

The virtual machine operates under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor and includes no bundled local disk storage or hardware GPU accelerators. Disk I/O relies entirely on remote storage, such as Azure Premium Storage. Networking configurations provide standard virtualized connectivity without complimentary public IPv4 addresses bundled by default.

Benchmark testing positions this instance within the mid-range tier across multi-threaded tests, recording a PassMark CPU score of 27099.51 and a stress-ng multi-core result of 16553.78. Memory bandwidth measures 132.44 GB/sec for large un-cached reads and 54.19 GB/sec for writes. The platform delivers strong single-threaded data processing, achieving 35.53 GB/sec in gzip compression and 14.66 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression, placing in the upper quartile. Driven by AMX instruction sets, text generation using small 135M language models reached 338.07 tokens per second, ranking in the top tier.

The 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM configuration delivers balanced resource density for workloads that do not demand excessive memory footprints or dedicated accelerator hardware. The primary architectural tradeoff is the absence of local ephemeral scratch storage, meaning IOPS-bound applications depend strictly on network-attached block storage performance. Suitable workloads include enterprise web serving, Redis caching, microservices backends, and lightweight CPU-based inference pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure D16s_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor running at 4.2 GHz. The instance provides 16 dedicated vCPUs across 8 physical cores alongside 64.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a standard 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio. It includes 480 MB of L3 cache and supports Intel AMX and AVX-512 instruction sets. The instance lacks local ephemeral storage and GPU acceleration, relying on remote network volumes for persistent data. In benchmark evaluations, the platform demonstrates steady mid-range performance with a PassMark CPU score of 27099.51 and 28.32 million Redis set operations per second. It displays above-average single-core throughput in gzip compression alongside top-tier text generation for lightweight 135M parameter language models at 338.07 tokens per second. The instance is suited for enterprise applications, caching layers, and web application serving.
